version.changelog:
Initial public release of WorthClip YouTube Video Scoring skill.

- Score YouTube videos from 1–10 based on your learning goals and persona using AI.
- Get AI-generated video summaries and alignment analysis.
- View a personalized, scored video feed with filters (score, verdict, pagination).
- Manage and track YouTube channels relevant to your interests.
- Check your current API usage and rate limits.
- Requires a WorthClip API key for access.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (YouTube scoring via WorthClip) is plausible and the runtime instructions mostly align, but there are metadata inconsistencies and a few details you should verify before installing or supplying an API key.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to call a WorthClip API to score YouTube videos and the SKILL.md shows endpoints and commands that match that purpose. Requesting a WORTHCLIP_API_KEY is coherent with the stated functionality. However, registry-level metadata (the top-level requirements block) lists no required env vars or primary credential while the SKILL.md metadata declares primaryEnv: WORTHCLIP_API_KEY and requires curl/jq — this metadata mismatch is unexplained and should be corrected/clarified. Also the API base URL (greedy-mallard-11.convex.site) is not obviously the worthclip.com domain; that could be a legitimate proxy or deployment but should be verified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md directs the agent to run three provided bash scripts (score.sh, feed.sh, usage.sh) which submit video IDs, poll for results, fetch feeds, and query usage — all consistent with the described capability. The instructions do not ask the agent to read arbitrary local files or unrelated environment variables; they explicitly require setting WORTHCLIP_API_KEY. Because this is script-based, review the script contents before execution to confirm no unexpected behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no downloaded artifacts; the skill is delivered as scripts and an instruction file. That is lower risk than remote installs. No extract/download URLs are used. The scripts will execute network calls (expected for an API integration).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md declares and requires a WORTHCLIP_API_KEY (reasonable and proportionate for this API integration). But the registry metadata shown elsewhere lists no required env or primary credential — an inconsistency that may indicate stale or incorrect packaging. You should confirm which metadata is authoritative before providing secrets. Also verify that the API key will be used only for the WorthClip service and not transmitted to other endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always: true (no permanent inclusion) which is good. However, disableModelInvocation is not set, so the model could invoke the skill autonomously. Autonomous invocation combined with an API key allows the model to send user-provided data (video IDs, personas) to the external API without an explicit user action; consider whether you want that behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (calls a WorthClip API to score YouTube videos) but there are a few red flags to check before installing: 1) Confirm the authoritative metadata — SKILL.md requires WORTHCLIP_API_KEY and curl/jq but the registry listing omitted those; ensure you only provide the key if the SKILL.md is accurate. 2) Verify the API base URL (greedy-mallard-11.convex.site) maps to WorthClip or an official WorthClip endpoint/proxy; do not give your key to unfamiliar domains. 3) Inspect the three scripts (scripts/score.sh, feed.sh, scripts/usage.sh) to ensure they only call the documented endpoints and do not exfiltrate extra data. 4) If you want to prevent the model from calling the skill autonomously, disable model invocation or require user confirmation before use. 5) Use a least-privilege or ephemeral API key if possible, and avoid exporting long-lived credentials globally.
